\caption{Causal hyperparameter-tuning battery extended with the spectral-kNN analog family (\textit{italic} rows). All arms share one out-of-sample panel ($n = 218{,}934$ thirty-minute bars, 100 walk-forward chunks with a 24{,}000-bar warm-up halo, pooled per bar) and one comparator: OLS on HAR $+$ calendar with no exogenous features (the production ridge path at $\alpha = 0$, exact OLS, per-bar refit), QLIKE $= 0.13415$. OOS-$R^2$ is measured against that incumbent, so $>0$ means the arm beats it. DM is a Diebold--Mariano test on per-bar QLIKE loss with HAC standard errors; negative $t$ favours the arm. The spectral-kNN arms compose a residualizer (identity, or OLS with the per-window identifiability mask) with a $W$-bar view of the target path concatenated to the bucket's non-target-derived feature row, matched by Gaussian-weighted $k$NN either directly (passthrough) or after a $d$-dimensional Laplacian embedding. Best QLIKE and best OOS-$R^2$ in bold. The dotted rule marks where arms stop beating the incumbent: every row above it has QLIKE below 0.13415, every row below is worse. Of 32 spectral arms, 8 beat the incumbent; the best ranks 21 of 98. The empty-exog bucket (SUBGROUPS key \texttt{baseline}) is displayed as \emph{no-exog (HAR only)} so it is not confused with the incumbent row; the underlying key is unchanged in the CSV. \textbf{Provenance:} the causal-tuned arms are audit-signed; the spectral-kNN arms are NOT --- they were run from an unsigned spec outside the submission journal, and cells whose unpenalized design went singular ($\mathrm{MZ}\text{-}\beta < 0.1$) are excluded.}
